question: Which river flows through the birthplace of the author of 'The Metamorphosis'?
context: Franz Kafka
Franz Kafka was a German-speaking Bohemian novelist and short-story writer, widely regarded as one of the major figures of 20th-century literature.
His works include the novella 'The Metamorphosis' published in 1915.
Kafka was born into a middle-class Ashkenazi Jewish family in Prague, the capital of the Kingdom of Bohemia.
Prague
Prague is the capital and largest city of the Czech Republic.
The city is situated on the Vltava River in central Bohemia.
It has been a political, cultural, and economic hub of central Europe for over a millennium.
The Metamorphosis
The Metamorphosis is a novella written by Franz Kafka first published in 1915.
One of Kafka's best-known works, it tells the story of salesman Gregor Samsa.
The story has been widely discussed among literary critics.
Danube
The Danube is the second-longest river in Europe, after the Volga in Russia.
It flows through central and southeastern Europe to the Black Sea.
The Danube passes through four capital cities: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest, and Belgrade.
Vltava
The Vltava is the longest river within the Czech Republic.
It runs northward from its source in Šumava through Český Krumlov, České Budějovice, and Prague.
It merges into the Elbe at Mělník.
Bohemia
Bohemia is the westernmost and largest historical region of the Czech lands.
In a broader sense, it often refers to the entire Czech territory.
Bohemia was a kingdom in the Holy Roman Empire and subsequently a province in the Habsburg Empire.
Gregor Samsa
Gregor Samsa is a fictional character and the protagonist of Franz Kafka's 1915 novella The Metamorphosis.
Gregor wakes up one morning to find himself transformed into an insect-like creature.
He struggles to adapt to his new condition while his family reacts with horror.
Elbe
The Elbe is one of the major rivers of Central Europe.
It rises in the Giant Mountains of the northern Czech Republic before traversing Bohemia and Germany.
It flows into the North Sea at Cuxhaven.
Czech Republic
The Czech Republic, also known as Czechia, is a landlocked country in Central Europe.
Historically known as Bohemia, it is bordered by Austria, Germany, Poland, and Slovakia.
Its capital and largest city is Prague.
Rhine
The Rhine is one of the major European rivers.
It begins in the Swiss canton of Graubünden in the southeastern Swiss Alps.
The Rhine flows through Germany and the Netherlands before emptying into the North Sea.

question: What is the capital of the country where the physicist who proposed the uncertainty principle was born?
context: Werner Heisenberg
Werner Karl Heisenberg was a German theoretical physicist and one of the key pioneers of quantum mechanics.
He is best known for the uncertainty principle, introduced in 1927.
Heisenberg was awarded the 1932 Nobel Prize in Physics.
Germany
Germany is a country in Central Europe.
Berlin is the capital and largest city of Germany by both area and population.
It is the second-most populous country in Europe after Russia.
Uncertainty principle
In quantum mechanics, the uncertainty principle is any of a variety of mathematical inequalities.
It asserts a fundamental limit to the precision with which certain pairs of physical properties can be known.
It was published by Werner Heisenberg in 1927.
Munich
Munich is the capital and most populous city of the German state of Bavaria.
It is the third-largest city in Germany, after Berlin and Hamburg.
Heisenberg studied physics at the University of Munich under Arnold Sommerfeld.
Berlin
Berlin is the capital and largest city of Germany by both area and population.
Its 3.85 million inhabitants make it the European Union's most populous city according to population within city limits.
The city is also one of Germany's 16 federal states.
Niels Bohr
Niels Henrik David Bohr was a Danish physicist who made foundational contributions to understanding atomic structure.
He developed the Bohr model of the atom and received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1922.
Bohr was born and died in Copenhagen, Denmark.
Copenhagen
Copenhagen is the capital and most populous city of Denmark.
The city had a population of 660,842 in 2024.
It forms the core of the wider urban area of Copenhagen.
Quantum mechanics
Quantum mechanics is a fundamental theory in physics that will describe the physical properties of nature at atomic scales.
It is the foundation of all quantum physics including quantum chemistry and quantum field theory.
It developed in the early 20th century.
Max Planck
Max Karl Ernst Ludwig Planck was a German theoretical physicist whose discovery of energy quanta won him the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1918.
As a theoretical physicist, Planck made many contributions to physics.
He was born in Kiel, Duchy of Holstein.
Vienna
Vienna is the national capital, largest city, and one of nine states of Austria.
It is located in the eastern part of Austria and is close to the borders of the Czech Republic, Slovakia, and Hungary.
It was the home of Erwin Schrödinger.
